findings.title: Step 3.2's pre-move check restates the write gate's refusal list with no held copy, so the two can diverge silently
findings.recommendation: The walk made Step 3.2 'run the same checks against the composed deferrals BEFORE the move'. No engine surface runs the archive write gate before the move (orbit emit archive resolves only the archived directory, emit-composition.ts:774-791, and there is no dry-run), so the body must carry the refusal list itself — seven refusals, one of them a fence-aware line scan — in prose an adopter's installed skill can read. A second statement of a rule with no parity check is the rule-stated-twice pattern R-crc-14 exists for. State the refusal list ONCE as a fenced production in the ADDED requirement, carry it into Step 3.2 as a CHECKED MIRROR held byte-equal by a parity test (the pattern the review and walk bodies already use), and add the mirror and its parity test to task 2.2 / 2.8.

walk_entry.title: Every deferral refusal lands AFTER the Step 5 move, and an id-less marked task is unfixable there without editing the archived tasks.md

findings.title: Bulk archive's own task count still classes a change whose only open tasks are validations as incomplete
findings.recommendation: The walk added Step 3.2 per change to bulk archive, but bulk archive classifies readiness by its own count (bulk-archive-change.ts:44-46 counts every `- [ ]`) and offers 'Archive only N ready changes (skip incomplete)' (:115). A change whose only unchecked tasks carry `(User-validation` is listed as incomplete and can be skipped before its Step 3.2 is ever reached — the exact prompt the single archive's Step 3 edit removes. Extend the requirement's bulk sentence and task 2.6: bulk archive's task count excludes the marked tasks Step 3.2 owns, as the single archive's Step 3 does, and add the case to the bulk scenario.

walk_entry.title: Bulk archive has no concrete integration for the new closure contract

findings.title: The walk's fingerprint re-stamp reordered .openspec.yaml outside every entry's edit record
findings.recommendation: git diff 7b1a0711 shows the `architecture:` block moved above `base_fingerprints`, rewritten by walk 1's `orbit fingerprint` run (content unchanged, fingerprints kept). A record gap, not a defect: name the re-stamp in the next log that edits the metadata, or leave it.

commentary: Graded the twelve owed entries over each sweep scope against the files at HEAD, then ran the proposal passes over the union. Ten landed as claimed: the A ruling reads consistently across spec, proposal, design, tasks and the explore pointers, and the residue that still says FORWARD is history (explore.md, design D5's account of the replaced draft). Both regressions are the walk's own new mechanism, and both come from one move: the walk extended a rule to a second site without checking how that site reads the same input. The pre-move check copies the engine's refusals into a body that has no engine to call, and bulk archive gained the new step while keeping the old count that gates entry to it.
